text:
Amy: quick RFC follow-up re: soft-preempt mode for dedicated pools. TL;DR — proposal: add an operator->runtime 'soft_preempt' token flow so operator can ask runtime to gracefully shed new admissions from selected nodes instead of hard-killing. want feedback on tradeoffs and rollout plan.

Jason: sounds useful. main worry is admission fairness + warmup-credit gaming. if soft nodes still hand out warmup tokens, tenants could pin.

Amy: agreed. operator-issued token should reduce admission score and stop granting warmup credits. existing leases stay running; token only affects new lease admission and prewarm behavior.

Sven: how does this surface in metrics? need early warning if nodes aren't draining. also we should consider model-level drain hooks for KV/cache flush.

Neha: can we reuse warmup accounting? my thought: set node.warmup_allowed=false when token set, and emit node.soft_preempt.inflight gauge. operator watches that + ttl to decide force-terminate.

Jason: sketch of operator->runtime API (pseudo):

```
soft_preempt {
  node_id: string
  token_id: string
  start_ts: int
  ttl_sec: int
  priority_impact: float  # 0..1 reduces admission score
}
```

Runtime behavior: mark node as draining, stop granting warmup credits, lower admission score by priority_impact, continue serving inflight requests, expose metrics `node.soft_preempt.inflight` and `node.soft_preempt.ttl_left`, call per-model drain hook to persist/serialize caches; emit `soft_preempt_drain_complete` when drain hits zero or TTL expired. Operator then either clears token or issues forced eviction.

Sven: what about preempt-shielded tenants (paid customers with shield)? operator must avoid choosing nodes with their affinity labels. if a soft token accidentally hits a shielded tenant, we need rapid rollback.

Amy: operator selection heuristics: prefer nodes with no preempt-shield label, and have option to dry-run token (no admission change, just metrics) for canary.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created issue https://git.internal/redwood/ops/soft-preempt-proto (link)

Neha: observability checklist: node.soft_preempt.active (bool), node.soft_preempt.inflight (gauge), node.soft_preempt.ttl_left (gauge), alert if inflight > X for > ttl_threshold. also add dashboard row in pool page showing soft-preempt tokens and affected nodes.

Jason: edge-case: multi-model pods where one model's KV flush blocks others -> TTL enforced kill could produce subtle consistency issues. mitigation: per-model drain API and operator can request model-swap to fallback variant before TTL. also add a soft_preempt_bypass flag for emergency (human-confirmed) to force immediate eviction if needed.

Sven: performance note — lowering admission score may cause admission thrash if operator marks many nodes simultaneously. recommend operator apply tokens incrementally (canary 1 -> 3 -> 10% of pool) and watch headroom metrics.

Amy: rollout plan suggestion:
- write RFC appendix describing token schema + runtime contract (Amy)
- POC: operator sets token & runtime honors (Amy + Sven)
- telemetry + alerts (Neha)
- canary: token on 1 node in pool A for 30m, validate inflight flows and warmup suppression (Jason ops-runbook)
- extend to pool-level automated soft-drain scheduling after capacity planning window (later)

Jason: add runbook steps: how to revert (clear token), how to force-evict (operator CLI with confirmation), how to verify KV persisted. also add autoscaler gating so autoscaler doesn't treat soft nodes as free capacity.

Neha: +1. I'll scope dashboards and alerts.

Amy: thanks all — I'll draft the appendix and open a PR with the minimal API sketch. owners: Amy + Sven for POC; Jason for runbook; Neha for telemetry. ETA: EOW for POC sketch.

Sven: noted, will start a small harness to simulate 3 tenants, include one preempt-shielded.

Neha: :thumbsup:

Jason: one last note — console UX: show per-node "soft preempt" pill with ttl and inflight count so SREs can quickly triage.

Amy: yep will include in PR. closing thread, will ping when PR is up.
